newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown retains gains but seen falling-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown retains gains but seen falling-dealers.

text.p: The Czech crown retained Thursday's gains after the open on Friday morning but dealers warned that the central bank would probably relax its squeeze on liquidity early next week pushing the currency lower.
At 0715 GMT the crown was trading at 18.8 to the mark, putting it 4.2 percent below its rate before the central bank gave in to speculative pressure for a depreciation on Monday evening.
"I expect sometime later today or most probably early next week an easing of monetary policy," said Petr Kukla of Girocredit Bank.
At the same time as abandoning its policy of intervening to prop up the crown, the central bank raised the discount rate to 13.0 percent from 10.5 and held the repo rate at around 75 percent.
Dealers say the squeeze on liquidity, which has pulled the crown back from lows of around 20 to the mark, is unsustainable and harmful to the wider economy.
Kukla said he expected the central bank to cut the repo rate rather than the discount rate as a first move.
